children: The slump in Australian average home prices continued in October with prices down 1.2% on month, according to Cotality, their seventh monthly fall in succession. Capital city prices fell 1.4% and previous months were revised to show bigger falls. Shane Oliver, chief economist at AMP now expects a 15% top-to-bottom fall, revised from a 10-15% fall. The pace of the decline is now tracking at its fastest pace since 1980, he adds. More interest rate hikes than expected, rising unemployment, and tax increases on property investors will continue to drive the retreat, Oliver says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
